holidays.name: National Noodle Ring Day
holidays.description: A day for the gloriously retro noodle ring. Cooks shape pasta into a ring, sometimes baking it in a mold, and fill the middle with creamy, saucy goodness. Think of it as a fancy pasta donut that is also dinner.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It follows mid-century American cooking, when molded dishes were popular on dinner tables.
holidays.funFact: Molded dishes like noodle rings were a hallmark of mid-century entertaining. Cooks packed pasta, rice, or gelatin into ring molds so the food would look fancy on the table.

holidays.name: National Have a Bagel Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy a chewy, golden bagel. Toast it, schmear it with cream cheese, pile on lox, or go wild with a pizza bagel. Any bagel counts, as long as you eat it.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It celebrates the bagel, a ring-shaped bread with roots in Jewish communities in Poland.
holidays.funFact: A traditional bagel is boiled briefly before it is baked. That step gives it a shiny crust and dense, chewy middle.

holidays.name: International Mountain Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate the world's peaks, from towering ranges to local hills. It highlights how mountains supply fresh water, support biodiversity, and shape the cultures of the people who live near them.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly designated December 11 as International Mountain Day in 2003. The first observance was in 2003, and it has been held each year since.
holidays.funFact: Mountains cover about a quarter of Earth's land surface. Roughly half of humanity relies on them for fresh water.
